text:
Marta R.: Heads-up — PR #412 for the Optimize toolkit examples is up. It includes new batching + KV prefetch examples and a small migration checklist. Can docs take a quick pass?

Liam W.: Thanks — linking it: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412 :eyes:

James (eng): Quick note: the Go snippet in examples/batching.go uses the previous SDK call shape. I left an inline comment with the suggested builder pattern fix.

Marta R.: Copy. James, can you paste the corrected snippet here so docs can verify?

James (eng): Sure — corrected JS/Go bits below. The Go change is minor: use client.NewRequest().WithModel("redwood/opt-1").WithBatching(true) instead of the old NewGenCall().

James (eng): ```go
// recommended pattern
req := client.NewRequest().WithModel("redwood/opt-1").WithBatching(true)
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)
```

Kevin D.: I'll run a quick smoke locally against the example harness. If the snippet compiles, we can merge. Also flagged that the quant profile link points to the internal qprofiles/ directory which moved. Need a redirect.

Marta R.: Good catch. Docs-bot, can you add a TODO to replace the broken qprofile link and add a short note about "short sequence" profiles?

Sophia (docs-bot): TODO created: docs#412: update qprofiles link + add short-seq guidance. Assignee: Ana. :white_check_mark:

Ana: Assigned. I'll add a quick blurb under "Quantization profiles" describing short-sequence tradeoffs (recommend fp16 or 4-bit fallback for <64 tokens). Will also add one concrete example profile snippet.

Liam W.: For the batching example we also need to show error handling when batching exceeds SLO and falls back. Could be a tiny paragraph and an example showing the fallback policy config.

Marta R.: Agreed. Keep it short — a single YAML block demonstrating policy.

Ana: Draft for fallback policy:```yaml
routing:
  policy: prefer_low_latency
  fallback:
    - model: redwood/opt-1-lite
      reason: lower-cost-lower-latency
```I'll add to PR.

James (eng): One more SDK note — embedding examples used an older param name "embed_model". New field is just "model" and type is string. I updated the JS snippet in the PR.

Kevin D.: Ran the harness: Go example compiles after James' change, but the sample microbenchmark shows throughput dip if batching window is >50ms. Add guidance to the batching page recommending 20-30ms default for interactive apps.

Marta R.: Perfect — Ana, can you insert "recommended defaults" bullets: interactive: 20-30ms, high-throughput: 80-200ms?

Ana: Added. Also added a one-liner about KV prefetch that points to our prefetch cheatsheet (and added the missing internal link as a relative docs link).

Sophia (docs-bot): Preview build started: https://deploy-preview.redwood-inference.org/412 — note: build warns about two broken anchors (quantization -> short-seq and prefetch -> examples).

Liam W.: I'll take the anchors. Looks like short-seq anchor name changed from "short-sequence" to "shortseq" in the qprofiles page. I'll align the anchor and push a tiny redirect snippet.

Marta R.: OK. Once anchors are fixed and James' inline comment is addressed, I'm OK to merge. Let's aim to ship before end of day so platform can pick up sample for the next release.

Kevin D.: Approving once tests pass. Left a small comment suggesting to add a short note under the SDK migration guide about the rename of the embed param.

Ana: All done: fixed anchors, added short-seq blurb, inserted fallback YAML, and updated the embed param note. Pushed amend to the PR.

Sophia (docs-bot): CI: build success, lint warnings: none. Link check: 0 broken links. PR ready for merge. :tada:

Marta R.: Merging now. Thanks team! :thumbsup:

James (eng): Nice, will update the example harness consumers to use the new builder API tomorrow.

Liam W.: Quick post-merge: can someone add a short changelog entry under docs/CHANGELOG.md summarizing "Optimize toolkit: batching defaults, KV prefetch example, quant short-seq guidance"?

Marta R.: I'll add the changelog entry and ping growth.

Ana: Leaving a note in the PR for translators — the new short-seq blurb will need localization.

Marta R.: Great. Closing thread. Thanks all!
